Martin County School District education: More students were enrolled in schools in 2024-25
H. D. Maddox
Martin County School District enrolled 18,323 students during the 2024-25 school year, an increase of 53 students, or 0.3%, from 18,270 in the 2023-24 school year, according to the Florida Department of Education.
Data reveals that the majority of students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year were white, representing 51.9% of the Martin County School District total enrollment.
Additionally, the largest portion of students in the district are enrolled in elementary school grades, making up 42.1% of the total enrollment.
Martin County School District covers 31 schools within Martin County, with its main office in Stuart.
Among the 31 schools in Martin County School District, Martin County High School recorded the highest enrollment of 2,055 students in the 2024-25 school year.
Florida allocated about $30 billion through its main K-12 school funding program for the 2026-27 fiscal year, an increase of $735.9 million, or 2.5%, from the previous year. Funding rose to about $9,338 per student, up 1.6% from 2025-26.
